intro: A frozen parameter can have a nonzero gradient. The optimizer must preserve its value despite that gradient.
task: Apply SGD only to trainable coordinates and report their changes.
requirements: weights, gradients and trainable are matching vectors; trainable contains numeric 0/1. learning_rate is in [0,1].
Return {"weights": updated vector, "delta": updated-original vector}. delta=-learning_rate*gradients*trainable.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: One frozen coordinate
examples.output:
{'weights': [0, 2], 'delta': [-1, 0]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Both trainable
examples.output:
{'weights': [1.9, -1.7], 'delta': [-0.1, 0.3]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Both frozen
examples.output:
{'weights': [1, 2], 'delta': [0.0, 0.0]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Zeroing a frozen weight would destroy the value you intended to preserve.

explanation: Freezing is an optimizer choice, separate from gradient computation. Keeping masked coordinates unchanged supports transfer learning and staged training.
The delta output makes the choice observable. Zero learning rate and an all-frozen mask both give zero changes without modifying the original arrays.
